metadata.title: Week 7 KP02 ImageNet and AlexNet (guided version)
metadata.description: IDL 2026 Week 7 KP02; reasoning-led-teaching-deck 2.1; English, self-paced reading; manual advance, try before reveal

scene-root.name: Week 7 KP02 ImageNet and AlexNet (guided version)

scene-u01.name: Week 7 KP02 ImageNet and AlexNet (guided version)

p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title
p01-hook-title.text: How do we know one architecture beats another?

p01-hook-ctx.name: p01-hook-ctx
p01-hook-ctx.text: KP01 set the starting point. This unit asks: to compare two networks, compare them on the same exam and the same data.

p01-hook-exam-t.name: p01-hook-exam-t
p01-hook-exam-t.text:
One exam: ILSVRC, a chosen subset of ImageNet with 1000 classes of image classification.
Results are reported as error rates; the lower the error rate, the better.

p01-hook-q-t.name: p01-hook-q-t
p01-hook-q-t.text:
This unit answers three questions:
1. What is this exam and how is it scored? (ImageNet, ILSVRC, top-1, top-5)
2. What does AlexNet look like and where are its parameters?
3. Which new practices did it use? (LRN, overlapping pooling, softmax loss)

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-title.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-title
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-title.text: Are ImageNet and ILSVRC the same thing?

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-ctx.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-ctx
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-ctx.text: No. ILSVRC is only a subset that ImageNet picks out; the two differ by more than an order of magnitude in scale.

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t1.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t1
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t1.text:
ImageNet: about $15$ million labelled images
about $22{,}000$ object categories (collected from the web, labelled by people through Amazon Mechanical Turk)

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t2.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t2
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-t2.text:
ILSVRC (held every year since 2010)
about $1.2$ million images
$1000$ classes, about $1000$ images each
RGB, resolution $224\times224$
(the source's wording; original images vary in size, so this should be the input after resizing and cropping)

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-err-t.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-err-t
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-err-t.text:
Thinking ImageNet is ILSVRC.
In fact ILSVRC is a subset of about $1.2$ million images in $1000$ classes.

p03-top5-title.name: p03-top5-title
p03-top5-title.text: Why is top-5 more lenient than top-1?

p03-top5-ctx.name: p03-top5-ctx
p03-top5-ctx.text: One image often contains several things, so five guesses are allowed. Below, an imaginary image ([Added] illustrative numbers) shows how the two error rates are judged.

p03-top5-hd.name: p03-top5-hd
p03-top5-hd.text: The model's scores for six classes (true class: tabby cat)

p03-top5-r1-t.name: p03-top5-r1-t
p03-top5-r1-t.text:
The highest score is 'fox', not the true class.
→ top-1 is wrong

p03-top5-r5-t.name: p03-top5-r5-t
p03-top5-r5-t.text:
'Tabby cat' is among the top five.
→ top-5 is right

p03-top5-cnt-t.name: p03-top5-cnt-t
p03-top5-cnt-t.text:
Test $1000$ images with top-5 error rate $17.0\%$:
$1000\times0.170=170$ images miss the top five,
and for the other $830$ the true class is in the top five.

p04-eight-layers-title.name: p04-eight-layers-title
p04-eight-layers-title.text: What do the eight layers of AlexNet look like?

p04-eight-layers-ctx.name: p04-eight-layers-ctx
p04-eight-layers-ctx.text: AlexNet was proposed by Krizhevsky (supervised by Hinton) and won ILSVRC 2012. Its skeleton follows LeNet: convolution and pooling first, fully connected layers last.

p04-eight-layers-t14.name: p04-eight-layers-t14
p04-eight-layers-t14.text: depth 48 is half of the previous 96

p04-eight-layers-t24.name: p04-eight-layers-t24
p04-eight-layers-t24.text: sees all 256 maps from both GPUs

p04-eight-layers-relu-t.name: p04-eight-layers-relu-t
p04-eight-layers-relu-t.text:
ReLU is used in every layer except the last (faster convergence). The whole network has about $60$ million parameters and $650$ thousand neurons.
Results on ILSVRC 2010: top-1 $37.5\%$, top-5 $17.0\%$ — these are 2010 results, not the 2012 winning score (the source gives no 2012 numbers).

p05-two-gpus-title.name: p05-two-gpus-title
p05-two-gpus-title.text: Why are the kernel depths of layers 2, 4 and 5 only 48 and 192?

p05-two-gpus-ctx.name: p05-two-gpus-ctx
p05-two-gpus-ctx.text: A GPU of the time had about 3 GB of memory and could not hold the whole network, so it was split over two cards. Half of each layer's feature maps are on card A and half on card B (the per-card counts are derived from the totals, [Added]).

p05-two-gpus-why-t.name: p05-two-gpus-why-t
p05-two-gpus-why-t.text:
A layer-2 kernel connects only to the $48$ maps of the previous layer on the same card, so its depth is $48$ (half of $96$). Layers 4 and 5 are the same, with depth $192$ (half of $384$).
Layer 3 spans both cards and sees all $256$ maps, so its depth is $256$.

p05-two-gpus-alt-t.name: p05-two-gpus-alt-t
p05-two-gpus-alt-t.text:
Without the split (every kernel sees all $96$ maps):
$256\times5\times5\times96=614{,}400$, twice the current $307{,}200$.
This 'looking at only some channels' was later called grouped convolution, but it came from the memory limit, not from a deliberate design [Added].

p06-feature-sizes-title.name: p06-feature-sizes-title
p06-feature-sizes-title.text: How does the feature-map side go from 227 down to 6?

p06-feature-sizes-ctx.name: p06-feature-sizes-ctx
p06-feature-sizes-ctx.text: The source gives no side lengths; they are derived with the formula $\lfloor(n+2p-k)/s\rfloor+1$ of Week 6 KP07 ([Added]). The 3×3 convolutions use padding 1 and the 5×5 uses padding 2.

p06-feature-sizes-flat-t.name: p06-feature-sizes-flat-t
p06-feature-sizes-flat-t.text: $6\times6\times256=9216$ numbers are flattened and fed into layer 6 (fully connected, with $9216$ inputs).

p06-feature-sizes-n224-t.name: p06-feature-sizes-n224-t
p06-feature-sizes-n224-t.text:
The source writes input $224$, but $(224-11)/4=53.25$ is not an integer, so the window overhangs at the end (output $54$); with input $227$, $(227-11)/4=54$ divides exactly and the output is $55$.
This unit derives all sizes from $227$; it is also why AlexNet is often written as $227\times227$.

p07-practice-a-title.name: p07-practice-a-title
p07-practice-a-title.text: Your turn: weights of layer 1 and its output side

p07-practice-a-ctx.name: p07-practice-a-ctx
p07-practice-a-ctx.text: Work it out in your head (or on paper), then press Next for the answers. Biases are not counted.

p07-practice-a-q1-t.name: p07-practice-a-q1-t
p07-practice-a-q1-t.text:
Layer 1 has $96$ kernels, each $11\times11\times3$.
How many weights are there?

p07-practice-a-q2-t.name: p07-practice-a-q2-t
p07-practice-a-q2-t.text:
Input $227$, kernel $11$, stride $4$, no padding. What is the output side?
And if the input is $224$?

p07-practice-a-q3-t.name: p07-practice-a-q3-t
p07-practice-a-q3-t.text:
The input of layer 6 is $9216$ numbers and the output is $4096$ neurons.
How many weights are there?

p07-practice-a-a2-t.name: p07-practice-a-a2-t
p07-practice-a-a2-t.text:
$227$: $\lfloor216/4\rfloor+1=55$ (divides exactly).
$224$: $(224-11)/4=53.25$, rounded down $53$, plus $1$ gives $54$ (does not divide).

p08-params-ctx.name: p08-params-ctx
p08-params-ctx.text: The vertical axis is logarithmic: each step up is 10×, so the real differences are larger than they look. (Number of weights = kernel size × number of kernels, biases not counted.)

p08-params-conv-t.name: p08-params-conv-t
p08-params-conv-t.text:
The five add up to $2,332,704$,
only $3.8\%$ of the whole network.

p08-params-fc-t.name: p08-params-fc-t
p08-params-fc-t.text:
The three add up to $58,621,952$,
which is $96.2\%$; fc6 alone has $37,748,736$.

p08-params-tot-t.name: p08-params-tot-t
p08-params-tot-t.text: The whole network has $60,954,656$ weights, about $61$ million (source: about $60$ million).

p09-lrn-title.name: p09-lrn-title
p09-lrn-title.text: What does local response normalization (LRN) push down?

p09-lrn-ctx.name: p09-lrn-ctx
p09-lrn-ctx.text: Layers 1 and 2 apply LRN after ReLU: it looks together at the outputs of neighbouring feature maps at the same position.

p09-lrn-read-t.name: p09-lrn-read-t
p09-lrn-read-t.text:
$a^{i}$: value of the $i$-th feature map (after ReLU) at position $(x,y)$.
$b^{i}$: value after LRN.
The denominator adds up the squares of $n$ neighbouring maps:
strong neighbours → large denominator → $b$ is pushed down.

p09-lrn-hp-t.name: p09-lrn-hp-t
p09-lrn-hp-t.text:
Found by cross-validation:
$k=2,\quad n=5,\quad \alpha=10^{-4},\quad \beta=0.75$
$n=5$ takes $5$ neighbours, $i-2$ to $i+2$ ($n/2$ taken as $2$) [Added].

p09-lrn-warn-t.name: p09-lrn-warn-t
p09-lrn-warn-t.text: Common error: LRN is not the batch normalization of Week 4. LRN pushes down among neighbouring feature maps at the same position; batch normalization standardizes over a batch of data. Later architectures mostly no longer use LRN (see KP03).

p10-lrn-numbers-title.name: p10-lrn-numbers-title
p10-lrn-numbers-title.text: Why is the same 100 pushed down more when its neighbours are strong?

p10-lrn-numbers-ctx.name: p10-lrn-numbers-ctx
p10-lrn-numbers-ctx.text: Take five neighbouring feature maps at one position; the middle one has $a=100$. $k=2,\ \alpha=10^{-4},\ \beta=0.75$ (numbers are [Added]).

p10-lrn-numbers-rc-t.name: p10-lrn-numbers-rc-t
p10-lrn-numbers-rc-t.text:
With very small activations $\alpha\sum a^{2}$ is almost $0$ and LRN just multiplies by the fixed $2^{-0.75}=0.595$.
Example: the middle $4$ of $(0,3,4,0,0)$ becomes $4/(2+10^{-4}\times25)^{0.75}=2.376$.

p10-lrn-numbers-cmp.name: p10-lrn-numbers-cmp
p10-lrn-numbers-cmp.text: Strong features compete, like lateral inhibition

p11-overlap-pool-title.name: p11-overlap-pool-title
p11-overlap-pool-title.text: How does overlapping pooling differ from the pooling of Week 6?

p11-overlap-pool-ctx.name: p11-overlap-pool-ctx
p11-overlap-pool-ctx.text: AlexNet applies max pooling after layers 1, 2 and 5 (in layers 1 and 2, LRN comes first and then pooling). Window 3, stride 2.

p11-overlap-pool-l1.name: p11-overlap-pool-l1
p11-overlap-pool-l1.text: A row of 7 cells; window 2, stride 2 → windows do not overlap (Week 6 setting)

p11-overlap-pool-l2.name: p11-overlap-pool-l2
p11-overlap-pool-l2.text: Window 3, stride 2 → neighbouring windows share one cell (AlexNet setting)

p11-overlap-pool-calc-t.name: p11-overlap-pool-calc-t
p11-overlap-pool-calc-t.text:
Window $2$, stride $2$: $\lfloor(7-2)/2\rfloor+1=3$ windows.
Window $3$, stride $2$: $\lfloor(7-3)/2\rfloor+1=3$ windows; cells $2$ and $4$ are each seen by two windows.

p11-overlap-pool-use-t.name: p11-overlap-pool-use-t
p11-overlap-pool-use-t.text:
Max pooling follows layers $1$, $2$ and $5$; layers $1$ and $2$ do LRN first and then pooling.
The window is larger than the stride → neighbouring windows share a cell, hence overlapping pooling.

p12-softmax-title.name: p12-softmax-title
p12-softmax-title.text: How does softmax turn 1000 outputs into probabilities?

p12-softmax-ctx.name: p12-softmax-ctx
p12-softmax-ctx.text: softmax: $\mathbb{P}(y=\ell)=e^{o_\ell}/\sum_{j}e^{o_j}$ (1000 classes); here we use only three classes ([Added]).

p12-softmax-sum-t.name: p12-softmax-sum-t
p12-softmax-sum-t.text: $0.659+0.242+0.099=1$: the three probabilities add up to $1$.

p12-softmax-goal-t.name: p12-softmax-goal-t
p12-softmax-goal-t.text:
Training goal: make the probability of the true class $\ell$ as large as possible.
To write 'maximize' as a loss to minimize, the source and the standard form differ — see the next page.

p13-loss-title.name: p13-loss-title
p13-loss-title.text: What is the difference between minimizing −P and minimizing −log P?

p13-loss-ctx.name: p13-loss-ctx
p13-loss-ctx.text: Formula (8) of the source says 'minimize $-\mathbb{P}$'; standard multinomial logistic regression minimizes $-\log\mathbb{P}$. The direction is the same but the gradient sizes differ.

p13-loss-cmp-t.name: p13-loss-cmp-t
p13-loss-cmp-t.text:
$\mathbb{P}=0.01$ (the model is nearly wrong):
the gradient of $-\log\mathbb{P}$ is $0.99$, pulling hard;
$-\mathbb{P}$ gives only $0.0099$, almost no gradient —
it learns slowest exactly when it is most wrong.

p13-loss-std-t.name: p13-loss-std-t
p13-loss-std-t.text:
Same direction, but optimization is much easier with the logarithm, so practice uses the log form.
This unit follows the standard form and marks the difference from formula (8) of the source.

p14-practice-b-title.name: p14-practice-b-title
p14-practice-b-title.text: Your turn: gradients of the two losses and top-5 counts

p14-practice-b-ctx.name: p14-practice-b-ctx
p14-practice-b-ctx.text: Work it out, then check. The gradient formulas are on the previous page.

p14-practice-b-q1-t.name: p14-practice-b-q1-t
p14-practice-b-q1-t.text:
The probability of the true class is $\mathbb{P}=0.1$.
What are the gradient sizes of the two losses on $o_\ell$? How many times larger is the latter?

p14-practice-b-q2-t.name: p14-practice-b-q2-t
p14-practice-b-q2-t.text:
A model is tested on $1000$ images with top-5 error rate $17.0\%$.
For how many images is the true class among the first five?

p14-practice-b-q3-t.name: p14-practice-b-q3-t
p14-practice-b-q3-t.text: If layer 2 of AlexNet had 'every kernel sees all $96$ maps', how many weights would it have?

p14-practice-b-a1-t.name: p14-practice-b-a1-t
p14-practice-b-a1-t.text:
$-\mathbb{P}$: $0.1\times0.9=0.09$; $-\log\mathbb{P}$: $1-0.1=0.9$.
The latter is $10$ times the former ($100$ times when $\mathbb{P}=0.01$).

p15-misconceptions-title.name: p15-misconceptions-title
p15-misconceptions-title.text: What is wrong with these four statements?

p15-misconceptions-ctx.name: p15-misconceptions-ctx
p15-misconceptions-ctx.text: Judge each one first, then read the correction on the right.

p15-misconceptions-m1-t.name: p15-misconceptions-m1-t
p15-misconceptions-m1-t.text: 'The parameters are mainly in the convolutional layers.'

p15-misconceptions-c0-t.name: p15-misconceptions-c0-t
p15-misconceptions-c0-t.text: ILSVRC is only a subset of about $1.2$ million images in $1000$ classes.

p15-misconceptions-c1-t.name: p15-misconceptions-c1-t
p15-misconceptions-c1-t.text: In AlexNet $96.2\%$ are in the three fully connected layers.

p15-misconceptions-c2-t.name: p15-misconceptions-c2-t
p15-misconceptions-c2-t.text: LRN pushes down among neighbouring feature maps; batch normalization standardizes over a batch — different mechanisms.

p15-misconceptions-c3-t.name: p15-misconceptions-c3-t
p15-misconceptions-c3-t.text: Same direction, but the former has the smallest gradient when the model is most wrong.

p16-quiz-a-ctx.name: p16-quiz-a-ctx
p16-quiz-a-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks no answers, so the answers and explanations are written from this unit ([Added]).

p16-quiz-a-q0-t.name: p16-quiz-a-q0-t
p16-quiz-a-q0-t.text:
Which statement about the scale of ImageNet and the ILSVRC subset is correct?
A. ImageNet has about 1.2M images in 1000 classes; ILSVRC about 15M images in 22k classes
B. ImageNet has about 15M images in 22k classes; ILSVRC about 1.2M images in 1000 classes, with images of $224\times224$
C. Both are only the 10-class MNIST
D. ILSVRC images are grayscale $28\times28$

p16-quiz-a-a0-t.name: p16-quiz-a-a0-t
p16-quiz-a-a0-t.text: Answer B. A swaps the two; C and D describe MNIST (Section 1).

p16-quiz-a-q1-t.name: p16-quiz-a-q1-t
p16-quiz-a-q1-t.text:
What are the layers and the hardware setting of AlexNet?
A. Only 3 fully connected layers, single CPU
B. Eight layers: 5 convolutional and 3 fully connected, split over two GPUs because of the 3 GB memory limit
C. 16 layers of all $3\times3$ convolutions (that is VGG)
D. No fully connected layers, only GAP

p16-quiz-a-a1-t.name: p16-quiz-a-a1-t
p16-quiz-a-a1-t.text: Answer B. C is VGG (KP03); A and D have nothing to do with AlexNet (Section 2).

p17-quiz-b-ctx.name: p17-quiz-b-ctx
p17-quiz-b-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks no answers, so the answers and explanations are written from this unit ([Added]).

p17-quiz-b-q0-t.name: p17-quiz-b-q0-t
p17-quiz-b-q0-t.text:
What are the hyperparameters of LRN in formula (7) (by cross-validation)?
A. $k=0,\ n=1,\ \alpha=1,\ \beta=1$
B. $k=2,\ n=5,\ \alpha=10^{-4},\ \beta=0.75$
C. $k=5,\ n=2,\ \alpha=0.75,\ \beta=10^{-4}$
D. LRN has no hyperparameters

p17-quiz-b-a0-t.name: p17-quiz-b-a0-t
p17-quiz-b-a0-t.text: Answer B. C swaps the numbers; D is wrong because LRN has four hyperparameters (Section 4).

p17-quiz-b-q1-t.name: p17-quiz-b-q1-t
p17-quiz-b-q1-t.text:
Which is correct for the pooling, parameter scale and loss (formula (8)) of AlexNet?
A. Non-overlapping pooling 2/2, about 600 thousand parameters, mean squared error
B. Overlapping pooling with window 3 / stride 2, about 60 million parameters, 1000-class multinomial logistic regression (softmax)
C. No pooling, unlimited parameters, hinge loss
D. Pooling only at the last layer, about 1000 parameters, binary logistic regression

p17-quiz-b-a1-t.name: p17-quiz-b-a1-t
p17-quiz-b-a1-t.text: Answer B. The pooling, parameter scale or loss of the other options are all wrong (Sections 3, 4, 5). The standard form of formula (8) uses $-\log\mathbb{P}$.

p18-summary-title.name: p18-summary-title
p18-summary-title.text: One sentence, plain words, formulas: what to take away from KP02

p18-summary-ctx.name: p18-summary-ctx
p18-summary-ctx.text: Close the slides and try to say the one-sentence version yourself.

p18-summary-one-t.name: p18-summary-one-t
p18-summary-one-t.text: Architectures must be compared on the same data: ILSVRC has about 1.2 million images in 1000 classes and is scored by top-1 and top-5 error rates. AlexNet was the first deep CNN to win by a large margin (five convolutional + three fully connected layers, ReLU, LRN, overlapping pooling, two GPUs), with about 61 million weights, 96.2% of them in the three fully connected layers.

p18-summary-plain-t.name: p18-summary-plain-t
p18-summary-plain-t.text: ImageNet is like a huge picture encyclopedia and ILSVRC is an exam drawn from it. AlexNet took an overwhelming score by being deep, large and trained on GPUs; most of its 'memory' sits in the last three fully connected layers, while the convolutional layers in front act like eyes.

p18-summary-fix-h.name: p18-summary-fix-h
p18-summary-fix-h.text: Corrections and choices relative to the source

p18-summary-fix-t.name: p18-summary-fix-t
p18-summary-fix-t.text:
1. The source writes input 224, but only 227 divides evenly.
2. Formula (8) of the source minimizes $-\mathbb{P}$; the standard form is $-\log\mathbb{P}$.
3. Side lengths, weights and neuron counts are derived from the kernel sizes ([Added]).

p18-summary-next-h.name: p18-summary-next-h
p18-summary-next-h.text: The question for the next unit

p18-summary-next-t.name: p18-summary-next-t
p18-summary-next-t.text:
AlexNet has only eight layers and its kernels go up to a large $11\times11$. What happens if we make the network deeper and shrink the kernels to the smallest size?
The next unit (KP03) looks at VGG.

p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0
p01-hook-cue0.text: Remember first: architectures must be compared on the same contest and the same data.

p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1
p01-hook-cue1.text: The VGG, Inception and ResNet of the next units compete on this exam one generation after another; AlexNet was the first deep CNN to win by a large margin.

p01-hook-cue2.name: p01-hook-cue2
p01-hook-cue2.text: This unit has three parts: first the exam, then AlexNet taken apart, finally the three practices it used.

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-nav.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-nav
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 02/18 · §1 The contest ground · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue0.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue0
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue0.text: Look at the big box first: ImageNet is a very large image database of about 15 million images and 22 thousand categories.

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue1.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue1
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue1.text: Then the small box inside: ILSVRC takes only about 1.2 million images in 1000 classes — the data used in the yearly contest.

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue2.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue2
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue2.text: Check the scale by multiplying: 1000 classes times about 1000 images is of order 10 to the 6th, matching 1.2 million.

p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue3.name: p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue3
p02-imagenet-ilsvrc-cue3.text: So the two terms must not be mixed up: every 'ILSVRC result' below is measured on this subset.

p03-top5-nav.name: p03-top5-nav
p03-top5-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 03/18 · §1 Scoring · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p03-top5-cue0.name: p03-top5-cue0
p03-top5-cue0.text: Look at the ranked scores: the model's six scores for one image; the true class is tabby cat.

p03-top5-cue1.name: p03-top5-cue1
p03-top5-cue1.text: top-1 looks only at the highest score: fox is not tabby cat, so top-1 is wrong.

p03-top5-cue2.name: p03-top5-cue2
p03-top5-cue2.text: top-5 asks whether the true class is among the first five: tabby cat is 3rd, inside the frame, so top-5 is right.

p03-top5-cue3.name: p03-top5-cue3
p03-top5-cue3.text: Turn the rate into counts: a 17.0% top-5 error rate means 170 of 1000 images miss the top five.

p04-eight-layers-nav.name: p04-eight-layers-nav
p04-eight-layers-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 04/18 · §2 Outline · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p04-eight-layers-cue0.name: p04-eight-layers-cue0
p04-eight-layers-cue0.text: Look at the five convolutional layers first: kernels shrink from 11×11 to 3×3; the depth column is explained on the next page.

p04-eight-layers-cue1.name: p04-eight-layers-cue1
p04-eight-layers-cue1.text: Then the last three fully connected layers: 4096, 4096, 1000; the last has one neuron per class, then softmax.

p04-eight-layers-cue2.name: p04-eight-layers-cue2
p04-eight-layers-cue2.text: All other layers use ReLU; note that 17.0% is the 2010 result, not the 2012 winning score.

p05-two-gpus-nav.name: p05-two-gpus-nav
p05-two-gpus-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 05/18 · §2 Two GPUs · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p05-two-gpus-cue0.name: p05-two-gpus-cue0
p05-two-gpus-cue0.text: First the division of labour: each layer's feature maps are split in two, the upper half on GPU A and the lower half on GPU B.

p05-two-gpus-cue1.name: p05-two-gpus-cue1
p05-two-gpus-cue1.text: Most arrows stay inside one card, so layers 2, 4 and 5 see only half of the previous layer's maps — that is why the depths are 48 and 192.

p05-two-gpus-cue2.name: p05-two-gpus-cue2
p05-two-gpus-cue2.text: Only layer 3 has the red crossing lines: it sees all 256 maps from both cards, so its kernel depth is 256.

p05-two-gpus-cue3.name: p05-two-gpus-cue3
p05-two-gpus-cue3.text: Optional: without the split, layer 2 would have twice the weights; grouped convolution was forced by the memory limit.

p06-feature-sizes-nav.name: p06-feature-sizes-nav
p06-feature-sizes-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 06/18 · §2 Sizes · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p06-feature-sizes-cue0.name: p06-feature-sizes-cue0
p06-feature-sizes-cue0.text: First part: 227 through the first 11×11, stride-4 convolution gives 55; pooling window 3, stride 2 shrinks it to 27.

p06-feature-sizes-cue1.name: p06-feature-sizes-cue1
p06-feature-sizes-cue1.text: Layer 2 pads by 2, so the side stays 27; after pooling 13.

p06-feature-sizes-cue2.name: p06-feature-sizes-cue2
p06-feature-sizes-cue2.text: Layers 3–5 pad by 1 and keep 13; the last pooling gives 6, and flattening gives 9216 numbers.

p06-feature-sizes-cue3.name: p06-feature-sizes-cue3
p06-feature-sizes-cue3.text: Check the input again: the source's 224 does not divide evenly, 227 does, so this unit uses 227 throughout.

p07-practice-a-nav.name: p07-practice-a-nav
p07-practice-a-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 07/18 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p07-practice-a-cue0.name: p07-practice-a-cue0
p07-practice-a-cue0.text: Work out the three questions yourself: two on weights and one with the output-size formula.

p07-practice-a-cue1.name: p07-practice-a-cue1
p07-practice-a-cue1.text: Answers: layer 1 has 34,848; output side 55 for 227 and not exact for 224; layer 6 has 37,748,736.

p08-params-nav.name: p08-params-nav
p08-params-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 08/18 · §3 Parameters · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p08-params-cue0.name: p08-params-cue0
p08-params-cue0.text: First the five blue convolutional bars: layer 1 has about 35 thousand, the other four between 300 thousand and 900 thousand.

p08-params-cue1.name: p08-params-cue1
p08-params-cue1.text: Now the three red fully connected bars: one to two orders of magnitude higher; fc6 is the largest.

p08-params-cue2.name: p08-params-cue2
p08-params-cue2.text: Compare the two labels: convolution holds only about 3.8%, fully connected about 96.2%.

p09-lrn-nav.name: p09-lrn-nav
p09-lrn-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 09/18 · §4 LRN · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p09-lrn-cue0.name: p09-lrn-cue0
p09-lrn-cue0.text: First the formula: the numerator is the original output, the denominator measures how strong the neighbours are.

p09-lrn-cue1.name: p09-lrn-cue1
p09-lrn-cue1.text: How to read it: add the squares of the n neighbouring feature maps; the stronger the neighbours, the more the output is pushed down.

p09-lrn-cue2.name: p09-lrn-cue2
p09-lrn-cue2.text: The four hyperparameters come from cross-validation: k=2, n=5, alpha=10 to the minus 4, beta=0.75.

p09-lrn-cue3.name: p09-lrn-cue3
p09-lrn-cue3.text: Do not confuse it with batch normalization: what they push down and how they work both differ.

p10-lrn-numbers-nav.name: p10-lrn-numbers-nav
p10-lrn-numbers-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 10/18 · §4 LRN numbers · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p10-lrn-numbers-cue0.name: p10-lrn-numbers-cue0
p10-lrn-numbers-cue0.text: Case 1: the middle is 100 and the neighbours are 0. Denominator 2.28, output 43.9.

p10-lrn-numbers-cue1.name: p10-lrn-numbers-cue1
p10-lrn-numbers-cue1.text: Case 2: all five are 100. The same 100, but the denominator rises to 4.30 and the output is only 23.2 — strong neighbours push it down more.

p10-lrn-numbers-cue2.name: p10-lrn-numbers-cue2
p10-lrn-numbers-cue2.text: Case 3: with very small activations LRN is almost just a fixed factor 0.595 and barely changes relative sizes.

p10-lrn-numbers-cue3.name: p10-lrn-numbers-cue3
p10-lrn-numbers-cue3.text: This is 'strong features competing with each other': neuroscience calls it lateral inhibition.

p11-overlap-pool-nav.name: p11-overlap-pool-nav
p11-overlap-pool-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 11/18 · §4 Overlapping pooling · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p11-overlap-pool-cue0.name: p11-overlap-pool-cue0
p11-overlap-pool-cue0.text: A row of 7 cells and the Week 6 pooling: window and stride both 2, windows do not overlap.

p11-overlap-pool-cue1.name: p11-overlap-pool-cue1
p11-overlap-pool-cue1.text: AlexNet uses window 3, stride 2: the window is larger than the stride, so neighbouring windows share a cell (gold frames).

p11-overlap-pool-cue2.name: p11-overlap-pool-cue2
p11-overlap-pool-cue2.text: Used after layers 1, 2 and 5; in layers 1 and 2, LRN comes first and then pooling.

p12-softmax-nav.name: p12-softmax-nav
p12-softmax-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 12/18 · §5 Loss · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p12-softmax-cue0.name: p12-softmax-cue0
p12-softmax-cue0.text: The outputs of three classes are 2, 1 and 0.1: the larger the number, the more the class is favoured.

p12-softmax-cue1.name: p12-softmax-cue1
p12-softmax-cue1.text: softmax exponentiates and divides by the sum: 0.659, 0.242, 0.099, adding up to 1.

p12-softmax-cue2.name: p12-softmax-cue2
p12-softmax-cue2.text: Training aims to make the true class's probability larger; there are two ways to write that as a loss, compared on the next page.

p13-loss-nav.name: p13-loss-nav
p13-loss-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 13/18 · §5 Loss · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p13-loss-cue0.name: p13-loss-cue0
p13-loss-cue0.text: Define first: both losses want the true class's probability larger; one minimizes −P, the other −log P.

p13-loss-cue1.name: p13-loss-cue1
p13-loss-cue1.text: Plot the gradient size on o: −log P is the line 1−P; −P is the parabola P(1−P), close to 0 at both ends.

p13-loss-cue2.name: p13-loss-cue2
p13-loss-cue2.text: Look at the far left, P=0.01: green point 0.99, red point 0.0099 — when the model is most wrong, −P has almost no gradient.

p13-loss-cue3.name: p13-loss-cue3
p13-loss-cue3.text: So practice always uses −log P; the source's −P is a simplification and this unit follows the standard form.

p14-practice-b-nav.name: p14-practice-b-nav
p14-practice-b-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP02 · 14/18 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p14-practice-b-cue0.name: p14-practice-b-cue0
p14-practice-b-cue0.text: Work out the three questions yourself: the gradients, the top-5 count and the weights without the split.
